newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico Cetes rate pares falls on liquidity drain.
newsitem.headline: Mexico Cetes rate pares falls on liquidity drain.

text.p: Mexican overnight Cetes rates moderated initial falls to close down 75 basis points at 22.15 percent on Monday on a late liquidity squeeze, traders said.
"Although we opened down, sellers stepped in before midday and we reached session highs when the central bank drained a hefty amount of liquidity," a trader said.
Banco de Mexico drained 5.617 billion pesos through seven auctions, which it assigned at maturities of between one and 43 days.
Overnight Cetes rates had opened at 22.00 percent.
Traders said secondary rates gained in late trade because the central bank assigned auctions at longer maturities than usual.
"The central bank drained at longer term maturities again and to a certain extent they are setting the stage for the primary auction," another trader said.
Traders forecast increases of 50-75 basis points on bellwether 28-day Cetes rates at Tuesday's primary government securities auction.
Banco de Mexico assigned 28-day Cetes at 21.16 percent at last week's auction.
Dealers said forecasts of increased primary rates were based on continuing concerns the Federal Open Market Committee may raise U.S. interest rates at its March 25 meeting.
"Amid fears that U.S. rates will increase, investors bail out of Mexico and go liquid," a dealer said.
Overnight rates on bank paper, meanwhile, ended off 80 basis points at 24.10 percent.
Liquidity of 267 million pesos was scheduled to return to the system on Tuesday from prior central bank participation in the secondary market.
